sentence: Nobody can find the API keys section; it is buried at the bottom of the settings page.

reviewer_notes.codebase_facts: Next.js 15.3 app router, React 19, Tailwind v4 @theme inline, shadcn new-york/zinc primitives, Geist Sans/Mono via next/font, light-first :root with .dark opt-in, left rail (hidden <md) + top header, settings sub-nav tab strip (General / Members / Billing / Security) in components/settings-nav.tsx; only /settings/billing and /settings/members routes exist.
reviewer_notes.premise_check: There is NO API keys section anywhere in the code (grep 'api key' over app/, components/, lib/ returns nothing; /settings/general and /settings/security routes do not exist). The sentence presumes a section buried at the bottom of a settings page; the code has no such section. The task will be run verbatim and the fix realised as: give API keys its own settings section reachable from the settings tab strip (own route, own tab), built with the project's primitives.
reviewer_notes.what_a_good_answer_does: Treat it as an information-architecture / findability fix on an existing settings area with a low budget: a dedicated, named entry in the settings sub-nav (aria-current, same tab pattern), its own deep-linkable route, page heading + description in the same hierarchy as Billing/Members, key values masked with a reveal-once pattern, reuse Card/Table/Button; no hero, no redesign of nav or theme, no command palette, no virtualised table.
reviewer_notes.forbidden_rationale: A nav transform, dark-mode redesign, hero/landing patterns or a command palette would all be out of budget for 'move a section where people can find it'.
